title: Correlation
subtitle: Spot positive, negative and no correlation on a scatter graph.

questions.correct: As one thing goes up, the other tends to go up too.
questions.feedback: Yes. The points go up from left to right.

wrong.label: As one thing goes up, the other tends to go down.
All the numbers on the graph are bigger than 0.
wrong.feedback: Positive here means the pattern goes up. It's nothing to do with the numbers being above 0.

wrong.label: Every point sits exactly on a straight line.
wrong.feedback: The points only need to go up overall. They don't have to sit on a line.

questions.prompt: Which describes graphs A and B?
questions.correct: A: strong negative. B: no correlation.
questions.feedback: Yes. A goes down close to a straight line. B has no pattern up or down.

wrong.label: A: strong positive. B: no correlation.
wrong.feedback: A goes down from left to right, so it's negative.

wrong.label: A: weak negative. B: strong positive.
wrong.feedback: A sits close to a straight line, so it's strong. B doesn't go up.

wrong.label: A: no correlation. B: strong negative.
wrong.feedback: A has a clear pattern going down. B has no pattern.

questions.prompt: Which description fits this scatter graph?
questions.feedback: Yes. The points go up and sit close to a straight line.

wrong.label: Strong negative correlation
wrong.feedback: The points go up, so it's positive.

wrong.label: Weak positive correlation
wrong.feedback: The points sit close to a straight line, so it's strong.

wrong.label: No correlation
wrong.feedback: There's a clear pattern going up.

questions.correct: Warmer days tend to use less heating.
questions.feedback: Yes. The points go down, so as it gets warmer, less heating is used.

wrong.label: Warmer days tend to use more heating.
wrong.feedback: That would mean the points go up. They go down.

wrong.label: Every day uses the same amount of heating.
wrong.feedback: The points don't stay level. They go down.

wrong.label: Each degree warmer always saves exactly the same heating.
wrong.feedback: The points are spread a bit, so it isn't exact. That's why we say "tend to".

questions.prompt: A scatter graph shows positive correlation between hot chocolates sold and gloves sold. Which sentence is right?
questions.correct: They tend to go up together, but that doesn't prove one causes the other.
questions.feedback: Yes. Cold weather could make both go up.

wrong.label: Drinking hot chocolate makes people buy gloves.
wrong.feedback: The graph shows they go together. It can't show why.

wrong.label: Selling less hot chocolate would stop people buying gloves.
wrong.feedback: That says one causes the other. Cold weather could explain both.

wrong.label: There's no correlation, because they're different things.
wrong.feedback: Different things can still go up together. That's positive correlation.

points.text: Correlation is the pattern the points make on a scatter graph.
Points going up from left to right is positive correlation, going down is negative, and no pattern is no correlation.
The closer the points sit to a straight line, the stronger the correlation.
Describe it with "tend to": pupils who revise for longer tend to get higher marks.
Correlation doesn't prove that one thing causes the other.
